facts.claim: Park et al.’s Generative Agents paper (2023): each memory is scored on how recent, important and relevant it is, and the model rates importance from 1 (everyday) to 10.
OWASP’s agentic threats guide (February 2025): require source attribution for memory updates, tracking where the assistant’s knowledge came from.
Chhikara et al.’s Mem0 paper (2025): for each new fact the model adds it, updates a memory, deletes one the fact contradicts, or changes nothing.
OWASP’s agentic threats guide (February 2025): limit how long an assistant keeps memories, based on how sensitive they are.
Anthropic’s help centre (checked November 2026): Claude users can see what it remembers about them, and edit or delete any of it.
Dong et al.’s MINJA paper (2025): an attacker who only chatted with an agent planted bad memories 98.2% of the time on average, in their tests.
Chen et al.’s AgentPoison (NeurIPS 2024): poisoning under 0.1% of an agent’s memory steered it over 80% of the time, while normal answers barely changed.
OWASP’s agentic threats guide (February 2025): keep memory snapshots so memory can be rolled back when something bad gets in.
OWASP’s agentic threats guide (February 2025): check new knowledge against trusted sources before it goes into long-term memory.
